query: Why choose Firecracker over gVisor/QEMU for sandboxing: summarize security, performance tradeoffs, residual risks, and a revocation/quarantine policy for malicious artifacts?

response.query: Why choose Firecracker over gVisor/QEMU for sandboxing: summarize security, performance tradeoffs, residual risks, and a revocation/quarantine policy for malicious artifacts?
response.answer: Firecracker offers faster startup times and better multitenancy than gVisor, but gVisor provides stronger security guarantees. Firecracker is lightweight, while gVisor emulates a full Linux kernel.

results.title: Sandboxing Untrusted Code
results.content: User-defined commands should be run inside a Docker container for users’ convenience: they could easily test these commands locally in the same environment. ## Docker Containers as a Sandbox Docker containers are not isolated from each other like VMs. In most cases and if you harden containers - they are safe. Some of SaaS services use Docker as a sandbox for untrusted code. But Docker containers need to be carefully hardened to be used as a sandbox: 1. Therefore I decided to not use just Docker containers as a sandbox in GolangCI. ### Create VMs in Cloud If almost every business uses AWS or Google Cloud or another cloud provider - we can use their API to spawn virtual machines, e.g. EC2 instances. 3. We can spawn and delete instances (VMs) by API but we still need to execute SSH commands to perform `docker pull` and `docker run`. Conveniently, we can use it with regular Docker containers. I’ve decided to test it on Google Cloud VMs. I did a build and static analysis of a sample Go project under normal and Kata Docker containers. ### AWS Firecracker Firecracker is a cloud-native alternative to QEMU that is purpose-built for running containers safely and efficiently, and nothing more. The `runsc` runtime integrates with Docker and Kubernetes, making it simple to run sandboxed containers. container startup time is very fast - no need to boot VM It looks promising and it’s used by Google App Engine for sandboxing. It worked 4-10x slower than raw containers: sudo docker = GO111MODULE = bash "time go mod download" sudo docker GO111MODULE = bash "time go mod download" There is a quantitive comparison between Kata Containers and gVisor. ### Google Cloud Run Google Cloud Run uses gVisor for sandboxing. ### AWS Fargate AWS Fargate runs containers in an isolated environment. I’ve tested its performance: Go building tasks are just 2x slower than in raw containers. If you don’t use a fixed pool of EC2 instance each container creation needs to pull Docker image. I would prefer gVisor because I can save 1 minute for each build on Docker image pulling and I would like to integrate it with Kubernetes.

results.content: 6.5810: Firecracker Adam Belay <abelay@mit.edu> 1 Agenda for today • Firecracker: Amazon’s serverless runtime • VM-based, but lighter weight than a traditional VM • Recall: Gvisor uses a libOS instead • Reminders: • No class Wednesday • Work on lab 3 • Propose a final project (alone or in a group of two) • Send us an email with your project idea and how you will evaluate it • After, we will meet and provide feedback on your proposal Recap: Serverless • Goal: Eliminate packaging and management (e.g., VMs or containers) • Instead, function as a service (FaaS): • Less time spent operating servers and capacity • Automatic scaling • Pay per-use of resources • Integration with source events / streaming data Challenge: Multitenancy • Must isolate for security • One function can not violate the memory isolation of another • Must isolate for performance • Must avoid the noisy neighbor problem • Firecracker takes steps to overcome both challenges Virtualization in Linux normally QEMU VM (Guest) KVM Kernel Module /dev/kvm VM Enter/Exit IOCTL() Firecracker replaces QEMU FireCracker VM (Guest) KVM Kernel Module /dev/kvm VM Enter/Exit IOCTL() What does QEMU do?
